messages:
ops-bot: Heads-up: Scheduled regional node evacuation for eu-west1 TOMORROW 02:00-03:00 UTC. This is a controlled drain to replace firmware on a subset of serving blades. Expect brief warmup latency for a subset of Dedicated pools and transient 5xx on very long-running streams.

tim (oncall): thanks. Is this limited to dedicated customers or will hosted API see any impact?

maria (sre): Primary impact surface: dedicated GPU pools in eu-west1. Hosted API routing will prefer other regions; routing policy will start preferring eu-west3 after 02:00 for new requests. There may be a 30–60s tail for some sessions.

jen (cs): Can we get a short customer-facing blurb I can send to impacted customers? Need one-line + 2-line detail.

sam (pm): Draft for status page and customer email below. Please proof.

sam (pm): "We're performing scheduled maintenance in eu-west1 on DATE 02:00–03:00 UTC. Some customers using Reserved/Dedicated capacity may see short elevated latency or brief failed requests while we rotate nodes. Our systems will automatically reroute traffic and we expect service to remain available. If you see persistent errors after 10 minutes, contact support."

jen (cs): clean. I'll add: "If you use IP allowlists, no changes needed. No model weights or prompt data will be modified."

maria (sre): Internal runbook snippets (paste into ops channel when we start):
```
- Preflight (T-90m): verify drain plan, confirm N+1 capacity, ensure autoscaler enabled for dedicated pools.
- T-15m: post statuspage "maintenance upcoming" and pin to channel.
- 02:00: start rolling drain on rack group A; monitor 95p latency, KV cache hit rate.
- If >5% error rate 30s rolling: pause, roll back this rack, open bridge.
```

tim (oncall): Also adding quick handoff note: I'll be primary until 02:20, then @maria takes over for the second half. Paging policy: if >3 pages in 10m escalate to eng-sre oncall.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Reminder scheduled: eu-west1 evacuation in 24h. Use /incident start <id> if you open a bridge.

jen (cs): Customer email subject suggestion: "Planned: eu-west1 maintenance — short latency impact possible" Body will include the sam blurb + support link and expected mitigation steps. I'll queue that for targeted customers using Dedicated in eu-west1.

maria (sre): Small tweak to statuspage copy (public):
- short headline: "Planned maintenance in eu-west1 — potential brief latency"
- details: "We will perform scheduled infrastructure maintenance in eu-west1. Some Dedicated customers may experience brief elevated latency or transient failed token streams while we rotate nodes. We expect automatic routing to keep APIs available. Maintenance window: DATE 02:00–03:00 UTC. Updates will be posted here."

sam (pm): Good. Also adding an internal snippet for eng-oncall channel so folks can paste quickly:
"Copy for Ops channel:
> Starting scheduled eu-west1 node rotation (02:00 UTC). Primary: tim (oncall). If you see >5% errors on dedicated pools or persistent regressions >10m, escalate to eng-sre. Customer CS contact: jen@redwood.ai. Status page: <status.redwood.ai/incidents/xxxx>"

jen (cs): I'll send the targeted customer note 1h before window and post the public statuspage at T-15. Will also attach the recovery steps for customers (retry backoff + switch region guidance).

maria (sre): Preflight checklist done - kernels verified on replacement blades, KV cache snapshot taken, autoscaler policy validated. Rolling image staged.

ops-bot: Posting scheduled maintenance banner to status page at T-15.

tim (oncall): Quick note for the bridge template when/if we open one:
```
- Bridge name: eu-west1-evac-<date>-<run>
- Runbook lead: tim (oncall) -> maria (sre) at 02:20
- Primary mitigation: pause drain, roll back rack, drain next rack after verification
- Customer comms owner: jen (cs)
```

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Maintenance completed (post-run) template:
"Maintenance completed: eu-west1 node rotation finished at HH:MM UTC. All nodes healthy, routing stabilization complete. If you experience persistent issues, open a support ticket and reference: eu-west1-evac-<date>."

sam (pm): After action items: collect logs for any 5xx spikes, validate latency graphs for 30m post run, and file a short post-run note on the status page (30–60m after completion).

jen (cs): I'll prepare a short customer follow-up message to send once we confirm stability.

maria (sre): Will post a final confirmation here when KV caches are warmed and 95p latency is back to baseline.

ops-bot: This thread will be pinned in #announcements and archived after completion. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
